answer: Make every identity earn its pearl: each agent stakes a small deposit that is slashed when its attestations disagree with the final ruling, so the fable of cheap sock-puppets collapses under real cost. Treat the trust graph as a web where each vertex is an agent and each edge a verified interaction; newcomers start at the periphery with low weight and gain influence only through sustained, corroborated work. Sybil clusters then stand out as dense, self-referential cliques with no outside edges, and their stake is forfeited.
